title: Tune on some warehouses, report on the others

blocks.text: A retailer solves a picking-route MIP for each of its warehouses every night and wants to tune the solver once for all of them. The team has already run every configuration on every warehouse model and stored the deterministic work in `work[(instance, config)]`. The first configuration in `configs` is the solver's default. The warehouses are split, before anyone looks at the numbers, into training instances, on which the configuration is chosen, and held-out test instances, on which it is reported.

With $`w_{i,c}`$ the work of configuration $`c`$ on instance $`i`$ and $`s`$ the shift, write down before you code: the score $`S_c(I)`$ of a configuration on a set of instances $`I`$ (the shifted geometric mean of lesson 5.4.2, given as `sgm`), the chosen configuration $`c^*`$ in terms of the training set, and the two numbers to report, each a ratio to the default $`c_0`$.

Write `score(work, config, instances, shift)` and `tune(work, configs, train, test, shift)` in `tuning.py`; `tune` returns `(chosen, train ratio, test ratio)`. When two configurations score the same on the training set, the earlier one in `configs` wins. The tests pass small tables; no solver runs. About eight lines.

from __future__ import annotations

import math


def sgm(values: list[float], shift: float) -> float:
    """The shifted geometric mean of lesson 5.4.2: exp(mean of ln(max(1, v + shift))) - shift."""
    return math.exp(sum(math.log(max(1.0, v + shift)) for v in values) / len(values)) - shift

         shift: float) -> tuple[str, float, float]:
    """Pick the configuration with the best score on `train` (ties to the earlier one; configs[0] is the
    default), and return it with its train and test scores as ratios to the default's."""

if __name__ == "__main__":
    work = {("w1", "default"): 900.0, ("w1", "fast"): 500.0, ("w2", "default"): 800.0, ("w2", "fast"): 950.0}
    print(tune(work, ["default", "fast"], ["w1"], ["w2"], shift=100))

cases.says: the choice is the best on the training set, scored on both sets against the default
a score is the shifted geometric mean of the configuration's work
held-out instances play no part in the choice
both ratios compare with the default, not with the best configuration
a tie goes to the earlier configuration, so the default wins a tie
the shift keeps a big ratio on a tiny instance from deciding the choice
